h1: Get found on LinkedIn by the people who buy
metaTitle: LinkedIn SEO Services for B2B Founders in India
metaDescription: LinkedIn SEO services for Indian B2B: one company page and five employee profiles tuned to the same twenty buyer queries, then tracked every month.
answer: LinkedIn SEO means tuning one company page and a handful of employee profiles so they surface for the same buyer queries inside LinkedIn search and on Google. In Indian B2B the founder's profile almost always outranks the brand page, so we work both surfaces together. From ₹30,000 a month.
takeaways: Six profiles, twenty queries, one map. A company page working alone in Indian B2B is a brochure nobody searches for.

LinkedIn search is **personalised by network proximity** — first and second-degree connections rank above strangers. That's why the founder wins and why connection strategy is part of the SEO, not separate from it.
The headline and the current job title carry the most search weight. The About section carries almost none for search and almost all of it for conversion.
Your LinkedIn profile is usually the second Google result for your own name. That's a page you control on a domain you never have to build.

sections.h2: Twenty queries, six profiles, one map
body: Most LinkedIn work in India is content work wearing a search label. Someone posts five times a week, engagement goes up, and nobody can name a single query the account now appears for.

We start the other way round. Twenty queries a buyer would actually type into the LinkedIn search bar or into Google — job titles they're hiring for, problems they're solving, tools they're replacing, the category name as they say it rather than as your deck says it. Then we map those twenty across six surfaces: the company page and five employee profiles.

Splitting them matters. If all six profiles say "helping businesses grow", you have one weak signal repeated six times. If the founder owns the category term, the sales lead owns the buyer's job title, and the technical lead owns the integration terms, you have six pages competing for six different searches and reinforcing each other on all of them.

sections.h2: Why the founder's profile beats the company page
body: This is uncomfortable if you've spent a year building the brand page, but it's how the platform works. LinkedIn is built around people. Its search results, its feed ranking and its notification logic all favour a human account over a corporate one, and the personalisation makes it worse for brands — results are weighted by how close the searcher is to you in the network. A person accumulates first and second-degree connections. A company page mostly doesn't.
In Indian B2B this gets even more lopsided, because buying committees check the founder before they check the company. A ₹40 lakh contract is a trust decision, and the trust attaches to a face.

So we don't fight it. The company page becomes the credential layer — clear category, real employee count, live jobs, consistent naming — and the profiles do the discovery work. Both get maintained; only one gets treated as the front door.

callout.title: The employee-profile problem nobody plans for
callout.body: You're optimising an asset the employee owns and takes with them. Agree that up front, in writing, and keep the company page and website as the things that don't walk out the door. We've seen founders discover this the hard way in month nine.

sections.h2: The fields LinkedIn search actually reads
body: There's a lot of folklore here. What's reliably true is that LinkedIn's people search matches keyword text most strongly in the headline and in current and past job titles, then in skills, then in the rest of the profile. Rank is then adjusted for network distance and activity. So the work is field-specific, not a general polish.
bullets: **Headline (220 characters).** The single most valuable text on the profile. Not "Founder & CEO". Something closer to "Founder at [company] — warehouse automation for Indian 3PLs | WMS, robotics, pick-path software". Job title, category, buyer, and the terms they search.
**Current job title.** LinkedIn treats this as a separate matchable field from the headline. If your title is "Chief Everything Officer", search cannot use it. Keep the funny version for your bio.

**About (roughly 2,600 characters).** Weak for search, strong for conversion. Only the first two lines show before the fold, so the qualifying sentence goes there — who you help, with what, and what happens next.
**Skills — up to 50, three pinned.** Skills are matchable and the pinned three appear high on the profile. Pin the ones from your query map, not the ones colleagues endorsed you for in 2019.
**Custom URL.** `linkedin.com/in/firstname-lastname-category` rather than the auto-generated string of digits. It's a small Google signal and a large credibility one.
**Featured section and experience descriptions.** Where you put the proof: a case write-up, a talk, a product page. This is also the only reliable place to put a link that isn't buried.

sections.h2: Posting cadence, without the daily content theatre
body: You do not need to post every day. The advice comes from people whose business is being seen on LinkedIn, which is not your business.

What activity actually does for search is keep the profile classified as active, which affects whether you surface at all, and generate the connection growth that improves your network proximity to future searchers. Both are achievable at two posts a week per profile.

We run a cadence of **two posts a week from the founder, one a week from each of the other four, and two from the company page** — with the company page mostly amplifying rather than originating. Every post is written against one of the twenty queries, so the archive slowly becomes a body of work about the same handful of subjects instead of a scroll of unrelated opinions.

Comments count too, and they're cheaper. Fifteen minutes of substantive replies on other people's posts moves more connection growth than a post that took two hours. We schedule that as work because otherwise it doesn't happen.

callout.title: Google is watching this profile
callout.body: For most founders, the LinkedIn profile is the first or second Google result for their own name. If your buyers Google you before a call — and in Indian B2B they do — the headline is doing double duty as a meta description you don't control the template of. Write it accordingly.

body: LinkedIn SEO sits inside [our organic social retainer](/social) — ₹30,000, ₹50,000 or ₹70,000 a month ex-GST depending on volume across channels. sections.h2: The baseline we freeze, and what the guarantee covers
body: On day one we write down two numbers from every profile in the set and freeze them: **search appearances** over the trailing 90 days, and **profile views** over the same window. LinkedIn reports both natively, which is why we use them — they're your data, visible in your own analytics tab, not something we compute and ask you to trust.

Search appearances is the honest leading indicator here. It tells you how often you turned up in someone's search results, and it responds to headline and title changes within two to three weeks. Profile views follow. Conversations follow those, and no dashboard will ever prove that link cleanly — we'd rather say so than draw an attribution arrow we can't defend.

The commitment is the same one we make everywhere: never a promised position and never a promised follower count. We beat your own frozen 90-day baseline within 90 days, or we keep working free until we do. It's the reason we cap intake at three new clients a month.

If your buyers search Google more than they search LinkedIn — and for most Indian B2B categories they still do — the bigger budget belongs in [SEO](/seo) or on the [B2B industry page](/seo-for/b2b), with LinkedIn as the trust layer that closes what search opens.

callout.title: The five people have to actually show up
callout.body: This is the one thing we can't do for you. If four of the five profiles go quiet in month two, the map collapses to a single founder account and the results halve. Pick five people who will genuinely give it twenty minutes a week, not five people whose titles look good on a slide.

faqs.q: Does LinkedIn SEO actually work, or is it just profile polishing?
faqs.a: It works because LinkedIn search is keyword matching plus network proximity, and both are things you can change. Rewrite the headline and job title against terms buyers search, and search appearances typically move inside two to three weeks. What it can't do is create demand for a category nobody is searching.

faqs.q: Should we optimise the company page or the founder's profile first?
faqs.a: The founder's profile, almost always. LinkedIn's search and feed favour people over pages, and results are weighted by connection distance — something a person accumulates and a company page mostly doesn't. Fix the company page for credibility, then treat the profiles as the front door.

faqs.q: How much do LinkedIn SEO services cost in India?
faqs.a: Standalone LinkedIn profile optimisation in India typically runs ₹15,000–₹75,000 as a one-off, and managed LinkedIn content ₹25,000–₹1,00,000 a month. We fold it into our organic social retainer at ₹30,000, ₹50,000 or ₹70,000 a month ex-GST, covering one company page and five profiles.

faqs.q: How often should a B2B founder post on LinkedIn?
faqs.a: Twice a week is enough to keep the profile classified as active and to grow connections steadily. Daily posting is advice from people whose business is being visible on LinkedIn. Two substantive posts plus fifteen minutes of real commenting beats seven posts nobody finishes reading.

faqs.q: Will my LinkedIn profile rank on Google?
faqs.a: Public LinkedIn profiles are indexed and usually rank on the first page for your own name, often above your own website. They rarely rank for competitive category terms — LinkedIn's domain strength doesn't transfer that far. Treat it as owning your name result, not as a substitute for your site.

faqs.q: Do you use LinkedIn automation tools for connections?
faqs.a: No. Automated connection and messaging tools violate LinkedIn's user agreement and get accounts restricted, which costs you the asset you just paid to build. We do connection strategy manually and slowly, targeting proximity to the buyers you want to be found by.
